issues.title: Trellis Frontend: Implement resilient Soroban RPC node failover and rate-limit backoff
issues.body:
The Soroban client in `lib/soroban/client.ts` relies on a single configured Horizon/Soroban RPC endpoint. When the RPC node experiences rate limiting (HTTP 429), network latency, or downtime during peak network usage, wallet transactions and contract queries fail silently or throw unhandled exceptions.

## Why this matters
Reliable node connection is essential for Stellar dApps. A single failing RPC endpoint breaks wallet interactions, proposal voting, and agent minting workflows for all active users.

## Tasks
- [ ] Implement a multi-endpoint RPC pool manager in `lib/soroban/client.ts` with primary and fallback node URLs
- [ ] Add exponential backoff and jitter retry logic for HTTP 429 (Rate Limit) and 5xx responses
- [ ] Implement active node health checks and automatic failover when node latency exceeds configurable thresholds
- [ ] Expose RPC connection status (connected, degraded, offline) to the wallet context and header status indicator

## Files to look at
- `lib/soroban/client.ts`
- `lib/stellar-constants.ts`
- `features/wallet/`

## Acceptance criteria
- Contract calls automatically retry against fallback RPC endpoints upon node failure
- UI gracefully displays degraded connection notice without crashing components

issues.title: Trellis Frontend: Add offline-first capabilities and background sync for PWA service worker
issues.body:
While `public/sw.js` and `lib/pwa-utils.ts` configure basic PWA caching, offline support is incomplete. Users who lose internet connectivity while browsing marketplace agents or viewing governance proposals receive standard browser offline errors.

## Why this matters
Many humanitarian and global users operate in environments with intermittent connectivity. Offline reading and background queueing of draft actions significantly improve usability.

## Tasks
- [ ] Configure Workbox runtime caching strategies in `next.config.js` for marketplace listings and static assets
- [ ] Implement Background Sync API via `lib/pwa-utils.ts` to queue pending form submissions (e.g., bug reports, feedback) when offline
- [ ] Add an offline banner component informing users when using cached data
- [ ] Write integration unit tests in `tests/pwa-utils.test.ts` for offline queue serialization

## Files to look at
- `lib/pwa-utils.ts`
- `public/sw.js`
- `next.config.js`

## Acceptance criteria
- Marketplace agents and documentation pages load from cache when offline
- Queued offline submissions automatically sync when connectivity is restored

issues.title: Trellis Frontend: Build IPFS metadata gateway fallback and cryptographic hash verification
issues.body:
`lib/ipfs.ts` uploads agent metadata to IPFS via a single gateway. If the primary IPFS gateway is slow or unresponsive, agent avatars, descriptions, and code manifests fail to load across the marketplace.

## Why this matters
Decentralized metadata must be resilient against individual gateway downtime while guaranteeing content integrity against tampering.

## Tasks
- [ ] Add gateway fallback array (e.g., ipfs.io, dweb.link, cloudflare-ipfs) in `lib/ipfs.ts`
- [ ] Implement SHA-256 / CID cryptographic hash validation after fetching IPFS content to prevent spoofed responses
- [ ] Cache verified IPFS metadata in IndexedDB via `lib/cache-manager.ts`
- [ ] Add unit tests verifying fallback progression when a gateway returns HTTP 504 or invalid content

## Files to look at
- `lib/ipfs.ts`
- `lib/agentMetadataSchema.ts`
- `lib/cache-manager.ts`

## Acceptance criteria
- Agent metadata loads seamlessly even if the primary gateway fails
- Tampered IPFS payloads failing hash verification are rejected with security warnings

issues.title: Trellis Frontend: Implement faceted search filtering and Algolia fallback for agent discovery
issues.body:
The agent discovery component in `features/agent-discovery/` relies on Algolia search. When Algolia API credentials are not set or when Algolia service is degraded, search returns empty results without falling back to local client-side filtering.

## Why this matters
Search is the core navigation path for users discovering AI agents. A failing search service severely degrades marketplace experience.

## Tasks
- [ ] Implement client-side fuzzy search fallback in `features/agent-discovery/` using Fuse.js or local regex indexing
- [ ] Add multi-facet filter controls (Category, Price Range, Stellar Network, Rating, Verification status)
- [ ] Preserve search query and selected filter facets in URL search params for bookmarking and sharing
- [ ] Add unit tests for search state synchronization and fallback switching

## Files to look at
- `features/agent-discovery/`
- `store/searchStore.ts`
- `app/marketplace/page.tsx`

## Acceptance criteria
- Agent search works seamlessly via client-side index if Algolia API call fails
- Faceted filters correctly filter results and synchronize state with URL query parameters

issues.title: Trellis Frontend: Add auto-reconnection and exponential backoff for agent telemetry WebSockets
issues.body:
The telemetry streaming connection in `features/agent-telemetry/` and `scripts/telemetry-ws-server.mjs` does not handle connection drops gracefully. If the WebSocket disconnects due to network instability, live metrics freeze without attempting reconnection.

## Why this matters
Real-time telemetry provides crucial monitoring during AI agent execution. Connection drops lead to missed status events and stale monitoring metrics.

## Tasks
- [ ] Add reconnection loop with exponential backoff and max retry attempts in `features/agent-telemetry/`
- [ ] Implement WebSocket heartbeat ping/pong mechanism to detect broken connections promptly
- [ ] Render visual status badge (Live, Reconnecting, Disconnected) on the agent telemetry dashboard
- [ ] Add unit tests mocking socket disconnects and verifying reconnect timer progression

## Files to look at
- `features/agent-telemetry/`
- `scripts/telemetry-ws-server.mjs`
- `app/telemetry/page.tsx`

## Acceptance criteria
- Telemetry client automatically reconnects after network drops
- Connection state indicators accurately update in real-time

issues.title: Trellis Frontend: Implement semantic versioning enforcement and visual diff viewer for agent versions
issues.body:
`features/agent-versioning/` tracks agent releases but lacks validation for semantic version strings (`MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`) and does not provide a visual diff tool for reviewing manifest changes between versions.

## Why this matters
Improper versioning causes compatibility issues for agent integrations. Visual diffing helps maintainers review code and prompt changes prior to release.

## Tasks
- [ ] Enforce SemVer rules using `semver` package when creating new agent release drafts
- [ ] Build side-by-side visual diff component for agent metadata, prompt templates, and plugin manifests
- [ ] Add rollback action allowing agent creators to restore previous stable versions
- [ ] Add unit tests verifying SemVer string validation and version comparison logic

## Files to look at
- `features/agent-versioning/`
- `app/create/page.tsx`

## Acceptance criteria
- Invalid version numbers (e.g. `v1`, `2.0`) are rejected with clear validation messages
- Visual diff view accurately highlights additions, deletions, and modifications between versions

issues.title: Trellis Frontend: Add governance proposal timelock execution and vote delegation workflow
issues.body:
The DAO governance interface in `features/governance/` and `app/governance/` displays proposal voting but does not support timelock queueing/execution or token voting delegation.

## Why this matters
on-chain DAO governance requires timelock delay periods between vote passing and execution to protect against flash loan attacks and allow user exit.

## Tasks
- [ ] Add proposal timelock status tracker (Pending, Queued, Executed, Expired) in `features/governance/`
- [ ] Implement Soroban contract call trigger for executing passed proposals after timelock expiration
- [ ] Build vote delegation UI allowing users to delegate voting power to trusted delegate addresses
- [ ] Add unit tests for delegation state calculations and timelock eligibility rules

## Files to look at
- `features/governance/`
- `app/governance/`
- `lib/governance/`

## Acceptance criteria
- Users can delegate voting weight to target addresses via Soroban transaction
- Queued proposals render real-time countdown timers until timelock execution is enabled

issues.title: Trellis Frontend: Build plugin permission manifest validator and sandbox isolation controls
issues.body:
`features/plugins/` allows extending agent capabilities with third-party plugins, but lacks strict manifest schema validation and privilege isolation checks for declared plugin capabilities (e.g., network access, storage permissions).

## Why this matters
Malicious plugins could exfiltrate wallet keys or user data if plugin permissions are not strictly declared, audited, and isolated.

## Tasks
- [ ] Define JSON schema for plugin manifests specifying required scopes (`network:read`, `storage:local`, `wallet:sign`)
- [ ] Build permission prompt modal requesting user authorization before activating high-privilege plugins
- [ ] Implement iframe/web-worker isolation wrapper enforcing restricted execution contexts for untrusted plugin code
- [ ] Add unit tests verifying manifest schema validation and permission denial paths

## Files to look at
- `features/plugins/`
- `lib/security/`

## Acceptance criteria
- Plugins attempting to execute unauthorized capabilities are blocked by the isolation wrapper
- Clear permission consent prompts are presented to users prior to plugin installation

issues.title: Trellis Frontend: Implement Merkle proof verification for on-chain agent execution attestations
issues.body:
`features/provenance/` and `app/provenance/` showcase agent execution proofs, but proof verification is computed server-side without client-side cryptographic Merkle tree root validation.

## Why this matters
Users and verifiers must be able to independently verify that execution logs match the cryptographic root committed to the Stellar ledger without trusting a centralized API.

## Tasks
- [ ] Implement client-side Merkle proof verification logic in `features/provenance/`
- [ ] Build visual proof tree inspector showing leaf hashes, sibling hashes, and root validation state
- [ ] Add Soroban state query to verify root hash matches on-chain commitment
- [ ] Write unit tests for Merkle tree reconstruction and invalid proof detection

## Files to look at
- `features/provenance/`
- `app/provenance/`
- `lib/provenance/`

## Acceptance criteria
- Provenance page displays verified badge only after client-side Merkle proof validation succeeds
- Invalid or corrupted proof chains display explicit cryptographic verification failure warnings

issues.title: Trellis Frontend: Implement multi-tier cache eviction strategy with IndexedDB storage quotas
issues.body:
`lib/cache-manager.ts` manages client-side caching but lacks Least Recently Used (LRU) eviction policy and StorageManager quota monitoring. Large cached responses can cause quota exceeded errors.

## Why this matters
Unbounded cache growth causes browser storage errors and performance degradation on mobile devices.

## Tasks
- [ ] Implement LRU cache eviction algorithm in `lib/cache-manager.ts` with configurable item count and size limits
- [ ] Add `navigator.storage.estimate()` monitoring to check storage usage against browser quotas
- [ ] Add automatic cache pruning when storage usage exceeds 80% quota threshold
- [ ] Add unit tests for cache eviction progression and quota handling

## Files to look at
- `lib/cache-manager.ts`
- `tests/`

## Acceptance criteria
- Cached items automatically purge under LRU policy when storage limits are approached
- Storage quota errors are prevented through proactive cache pruning

- [ ] Add unit tests for APY math, unbonding penalty calculations, and claim eligibility checks

## Files to look at
- `app/staking/`
- `lib/staking/`
- `lib/soroban/`

## Acceptance criteria
